articles.title: Creaking, smug … and a contender? Aaron Rodgers may yet get his Super Bowl farewell
articles.summary: The 42-year-old remains a polarizing figure. But the Steelers have a formidable defense and a quarterback who has seen it all before. Aaron Rodgers is nowhere near this season’s MVP conversation.
body: Rodgers looked more like prime Rodgers in the Steelers’ gritty 16-10 win over the Saints in Paris. He wasn’t satisfied with his side of the ball, telling reporter Molly McGrath, “I don’t think we played very good on offense today.” But Rodgers did enough to secure the win, including a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf in the second quarter. He later scrambled for a first down on third-and-six to secure the win.

Sure, there were points left on the table – the Steelers had several stalled drives and only scored one touchdown in four red-zone trips – and 16 points against a two-win team isn’t impressive. But the Steelers left France with a win, a 5-2 record and a ton of upside.
So here’s a crazy thought: Could Rodgers win a Super Bowl in his final NFL season?
points: But the Steelers have a formidable defense and a quarterback who has seen it all before.
Aaron Rodgers is nowhere near this season’s MVP conversation.

But Rodgers did enough to secure the win, including a 51-yard strike to DK Metcalf in the second quarter.

articles.title: ‘Even my best friend didn’t know’: Usman Khawaja reveals why he kept his rheumatoid arthritis a secret
articles.summary: Opener played through pain to establish himself as a Test cricketer. ‘I didn’t want anyone to use it against me,’ he says. Usman Khawaja has opened up on why he kept the rheumatoid arthritis that threatened his playing future a secret for his entire Test career.
body: The former Test star releases his autobiography, Sabr, on 10 November, which he said he wrote “for people who do love cricket and for those who don’t”.
“We are all human and go through the ups and downs of life. I go through the ups and downs of cricket and it gets accentuated because everyone gets to see it,” Khawaja said.
One key aspect of Khawaja’s career the public did not know about was the arthritis diagnosis at the age of 22 after the pain in his left knee was so great he couldn’t walk 10m to the bathroom.
Only regular injections kept him on his feet and able to play cricket. He still has them.

articles.title: ‘We’re not doing great’: Gilgeous-Alexander in tears after Williams suffers gruesome leg injury
articles.summary: Guard stretchered off court after apparent serious injury. Team will learn more about status on Monday. Shai-Gilgeous Alexander scored 34 points and the Oklahoma City Thunder stayed undefeated but they lost All-Star guard Jalen Williams to what appeared to be a serious leg injury during their…
body: Oklahoma City won their third straight game to start the season but lost three players to injury, including Williams, who went down hard on a drive to the basket with 1:14 left. The guard’s left leg gave way as he landed and his foot bent at an unnatural angle. The 25-year-old left the court on a stretcher with towels covering his injured leg. He covered his mouth with his hands when he looked down at the injury while Gilgeous Alexander and players on both teams appeared to be in shock.
“We’re not doing great,” Thunder coach Mark Daigneault said after the game. He added that the team would be updated on the injury on Monday.
Gilgeous-Alexander was in tears as he spoke about Williams after the game.

“I just feel bad for him,” Gilgeous-Alexander said. “It’s obviously going to be tough without a player like that. But he’s not gone for ever. He’ll be back better than ever, and we know it. We’ve just got to hold the fort down until he comes back.”

articles.title: Doha to Omagh - A 7160-mile journey for 'my World Cup'
articles.summary: After making a 7160-mile round trip from Qatar to Omagh to make history with Edendork, Neil Kilpatrick says winning the Tyrone SFC title is "my World Cup".
body: The round trip journey from Edendork to Healy Park in Omagh is around 60 miles.
But for Neil Kilpatrick, the journey towards helping his club to a first-ever Tyrone Senior Football Championship title was just a little longer.
It's just the 7,160 miles, to be exact, from Doha to Omagh as Kilpatrick made the journey from his teaching job in Qatar to line-out for his beloved Edendork.
It was a journey he had to make twice in less than a week after the first game ended in a draw, which meant a replay and a few hastily arranged long-haul flights.

articles.title: 'I'm not the one who picks it!' - Should Smith get PL debut after major win?
articles.summary: Ross Smith believes he ‘definitely’ deserves a Premier League debut on current form, having securing a second TV major title of the season at the Machineseeker European Championship.
body: Smith joined Michael van Gerwen, Phil Taylor, Rob Cross and Peter Wright as a multiple winner of the European Championship, following his 2022 success by defeating Martin Schindler 11-8 in the final in Dortmund on Sunday.

The Englishman's latest victory adds to September's World Series Finals success and moves him to a career-high world No 6 in the PDC Order of Merit, having also won two European Tour and two Players Championship titles this season.

Smith will have further opportunities in the coming months to add to his major tally, while the 37-year-old is hopeful that his impressive campaign will bolster his chances of being selected - if not qualifying automatically - for Premier League debut next season.

When asked whether he is deserving of a Premier League spot in 2027, Smith said in his victory press conference: "Yes, at the moment, definitely. At the end of the year, who knows? There's another three majors to come - it depends on what other players do.

articles.title: 'People don't want to go home' - England ready for must-win Samoa clash
articles.summary: England head coach Stuart Barrow insists his side remain positive of reaching the Women's Rugby League World Cup semi-finals, despite being 'blown away' in a 78-0 drubbing by Australia on Saturday.
body: Nineteen months on from a humbling 90-4 loss to Australia in Las Vegas, England suffered another heavy defeat against the same opposition after the Jillaroos ran in 15 tries during a one-sided contest.
England now travel from Perth to Wollongong for Friday's winner-takes-all clash with Samoa (6.45am GMT), where a victory is required to finish second in Group A and reach the knockout stages.

"There are some people in the group who were at Vegas and they're in the changing room saying 'this wasn't like Vegas, it doesn't feel like Vegas, you're not part of what happened at Vegas - this is different'," Barrow told reporters.

"Yeah, we didn't help ourselves and the scoreline's still big, but I think people have still got some positivity in there and people don't want to go home. They want to have this game against Samoa and give our best."

articles.title: Vikings are last unbeaten team as Chiefs lose - NFL week seven
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers lost in week seven of the NFL, leaving the Minnesota Vikings as this season's last unbeaten team.
body: Week seven of the NFL left one unbeaten team standing and few - if any - would have picked them out at the start of the season.
The Kansas City Chiefs were beaten at defending champions the Seattle Seahawks while the San Francisco 49ers also suffered their first loss.
But the Minnesota Vikings marched on to maintain their 100% record, and there were also big wins for the Cleveland Browns and Denver Broncos.
Kansas City and Seattle have not only won three of the past four Super Bowls, they came into week seven with this season's best offence and best defence respectively, in terms of total yards.

articles.title: Thunder star Williams stretched off with leg injury
articles.summary: Oklahoma City Thunder star Jalen Williams was taken off the court on a stretcher after suffering a significant lower-leg injury during their 108-101 victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.
body: Williams - a shooting guard who entered Sunday having averaged 18 points per game in his first 250 NBA contests - has been an All-Star and an All-NBA player already in his career, was a huge part of the Thunder team that won the 2024-25 NBA title.

He injured his lower left leg and saw his ankle turn in an unnatural angle in a drive with 1:14 remaining, with Williams immediately treated by medical personnel after going down underneath the basket on the Thunder's offensive end.

Williams' ankle was draped by towels before a stretcher was brought out, with players left visibly shaken by the incident and the game stopped for around five minutes before the Thunder completed their victory.
"Just feel bad for him," Thunder guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander said in a post-match interview, fighting back tears as he spoke. "Nothing more than that."

With towels draped over Williams’ ankle, players from both teams reacted with immediate shock and dismay as the stretcher was brought onto the court. The contest was delayed about five minutes before the Thunder secured a 108-101 victory.
